metadata.description: A storage provisioning policy a volume requests storage by: the provisioner, what happens on release, when binding happens, and what the class can do. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): its contract is the Kubernetes StorageClass object every CSI-backed provider exposes, so any of them publishes one. A storage class is published by a provider and selected by a volume, never ordered on its own; it is where the provider reports the `tier` and `capabilities` placement matches against.

name.description: The storage class name, unique within the cluster.

provisioner.description: The provisioner that handles volumes of this class (a CSI driver name).

reclaim_policy.description: What happens to the underlying storage when a volume is released: Retain, Delete or Recycle.

volume_binding_mode.description: When binding and provisioning happen: `Immediate`, or `WaitForFirstConsumer` to defer until a consumer is scheduled.

allow_volume_expansion.description: Whether volumes of this class can grow after creation.

tier.description: The governed `storage_tier` this class satisfies. A provider that exposes storage classes MUST map each to a tier, so tier-authored intent (name-selectable, requirements-authoritative; ADR-036) resolves against it. The class chosen for a request is recorded as a realized fact on the consumer side, never in intent. Governed vocabulary `storage_tier` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

capabilities.description: Capability advertisements placement selects by: IOPS, throughput, encryption, replication factor, snapshot support.

parameters.description: Provisioner-specific parameters (pool, fsType, compression). Opaque to the model; the provisioner interprets them.

name.description: The realized storage class name — the string value that Volume.storage_class references.

relationships.name: storage_backend
relationships.description: The storage cluster that backs this class (e.g., a Ceph cluster, a NetApp filer).

adopts.role: named storage provisioning policy (provisioner, reclaimPolicy, volumeBindingMode, parameters)

context.purpose: Names a storage provisioning policy — provisioner, reclaim, binding mode, capabilities — that volumes request storage by.
context.plain_description: The Kubernetes StorageClass construct: a named policy — its `name` and `provisioner` are required — saying which provisioner builds volumes, what happens to data on release (`reclaim_policy`), when binding happens (`volume_binding_mode`, Kubernetes-cased: `Immediate` or `WaitForFirstConsumer`), whether volumes can grow (`allow_volume_expansion`), and what the class can do (`capabilities` — IOPS, encryption, replication, snapshots). A volume asks for storage by naming a class; placement policies select classes by capability. Provisioner-specific parameters ride along opaquely — the provisioner interprets them, the model does not.
use_when: You need volumes to request storage by named policy instead of naming backends.
You need placement to pick storage by advertised capability (encrypted, fast, replicated).
not_for: The volume itself — Volume references a class.
The backing storage system — StorageCluster; the class is the policy naming what the cluster serves.
Host-local pools — StoragePool; a class is a platform-level provisioning policy.
works_with: Volume — volumes declare their class by reference.
StorageCluster — the storage cluster backing the class.
Machine.VM — VM disks select a storage class.
